chunks: And another is he who calls himself learned but is not so; he has gleaned ignorance from the ignorant and misguidance from the misguided. He has set for the people traps made of ropes of deceit and untrue speech. He has carried the Book according to his own views and bent the truth to his passions. He makes people feel safe from major sins and trivializes serious crimes. He says: 'I pause at doubts,' yet he remains plunged therein; and he says: 'I keep aloof from innovations,' yet he is immersed in them. His form is that of a man, but his heart is that of a beast. He does not know the door of guidance to follow it, nor the door of misguidance to keep aloof from it. So he is the living dead!
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a hypocritical scholar in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali characterizes this 'false scholar' as one who subjugates the Quran to his own whims (ta'wil bi'l-ra'y) and minimizes major sins to maintain social standing, a critique often linked to the Umayyad era's politicized religious figures. This figure represents the 'living dead' (mayyit al--hiyah), possessing the outward form of a human but the beastly heart of one devoid of spiritual insight, effectively confusing the path of guidance with the path of error. His condition highlights the Shia emphasis on internal sincerity and accurate understanding over mere outward piety or rhetorical skill.
